subject: On‑prem cluster: node scheduling, storage QoS & tenant isolation - next steps
messages:
From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@edgeworks.com>
To: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
Cc: kate.monroe@rockwell.io, ops@edgeworks.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster constraints and scheduling questions

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we kick off prep for the on‑prem cluster (Rockwell pilot), two items bubbled up from our infra and storage teams that we need to lock down before the sprint kickoff:

1) Node scheduling for mixed CPU/GPU racks — we have three rack classes (cpu-high, gpu-mixed, gpu-dedicated). We need guidance on Affinity/Taints strategy that minimizes preemption while preserving eviction windows for spot maintenance.

2) Storage QoS — Rockwell requires per-tenant IOPS ceilings (soft and hard) and a predictable eviction/retention policy for KV caches (rocksdb) vs model artifacts. Their ops team wants to avoid noisy neighbors causing degraded tail latency.

Can you propose a short runbook or config profile we can trial? I'll attach the site inventory and the initial performance goals.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call.

— Sam
EdgeWorks Systems

Attachments: edgeworks-site-inventory.xlsx, workload-goals.pdf

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: sam.ellis@edgeworks.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, kate.monroe@rockwell.io
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster constraints and scheduling questions

Sam — thanks for the details and the inventory. High level response below; I attached a couple of artifacts (prelim-sched-profiles.yaml and kv-cache-design-notes.md) that map to each item.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Node scheduling: use a combination of node taints + topology-aware labels (rack_id, zone_type) and pod affinity for stable placement of long‑running model servers. For batch/ephemeral workloads enable lower-priority preemptible classes with a graceful termination window (60s) and prefer disruption budgets for stateful model pods.
- GPU lanes: carve out a gpu-dedicated nodepool for latency‑sensitive inference (pinned GPU, 1 pod per GPU) and a gpu-shared pool for training/batch jobs (multi‑pod on GPU when using MIG/partitioning). Use kube-arbitrator settings to prefer packing on heterogeneous hardware.
- Storage QoS: implement CSI QoS classes (gold/silver/bronze) mapped to per-tenant StorageClass; enforce IOPS via provisioned LVM on local NVMe for gold and through QoS on your SAN for lower tiers. For KV caches, use an in‑node ephemeral cache with async snapshotting to object store + a small persistent rocksdb PV with priorityClass backing to avoid eviction during node pressure.

Security/compliance notes: KMS integration for model artifacts should be scoped per-tenant; audit log forwarding to Rockwell's SIEM over syslog + mutual TLS is recommended.

Next steps I propose:
1) Align on three scheduling profiles (latency, mixed, batch) — I included YAML examples.
2) We run a 48‑hour soak with traffic shaping to validate tail latency and eviction behaviour.
3) Neha will validate KMS/audit gaps; Lauren will coordinate Procure/contract for node labeling telemetry.

If that sounds right I'll schedule a 45‑minute working session this afternoon (I put a tentative slot on the calendar).

Best,
Hiro
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: prelim-sched-profiles.yaml, kv-cache-design-notes.md

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, sam.ellis@edgeworks.com, platform-security@rockwell.io
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster constraints and scheduling questions

Quick followups from compliance/security POV — copied Rockwell security so they have visibility.

1) KMS: we need to confirm if Rockwell will provide an external KMS endpoint (HSM/KMS) or if we'll provision a customer‑dedicated KMS in their VPC. For envelope encryption, we recommend per-tenant key wrapping and a rotation policy (90 days).
2) Audit logs: please confirm retention target (90/365 days?) and whether logs must be immutable. We can forward to your SIEM but retention outside Redwood implies S3+WORM controls on your side.
3) KV cache snapshotting: if snapshots contain PII/PHI we need explicit marking and per-tenant access controls — otherwise snapshots may be stored with lower encryption scope.

Can Rockwell security clarify the above before we start the soak so we can include controls in the runbook.

— Neha
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>

Thanks — useful questions. Kate / Rockwell security: can you confirm the KMS approach and log retention requirements by tomorrow morning? That will determine a small config change to the YAML and the snapshot workflow.

Action items we will own before the soak:
- Hiro: finalize scheduling YAML and pack the soak plan (traffic shapes + SLO targets).
- Karthik: prepare nodepool sizing and GPU partitioning recommendations (MIG vs dedicated).
- Neha: produce a short compliance checklist for KMS rotations and snapshot classification.
- Lauren: follow up with procurement on label telemetry and node tagging contract items.

If Rockwell can confirm KMS + retention, we'll flip the tentative calendar invite to a working session at 15:30 PT tomorrow and share the Drive folder with the artifacts.

Thanks everyone — attaching the site inventory for convenience.

— Hiro
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
